Cyber Attack on Thailand’s Payments System Disrupts Businesses Nationwide

BANGKOK — A large-scale cyber attack targeting Thailand’s central electronic payments network has disrupted transactions across the country, affecting businesses, consumers, and government services since early Wednesday morning.

The attack, which began at approximately 6:30 a.m., has caused widespread outages at payment terminals, mobile banking apps, and ATMs linked to the national clearinghouse, PayLink Thailand. Major shopping malls in Bangkok and Chiang Mai have reported long queues at cash counters, while smaller vendors in provincial markets have switched to cash-only sales.

“We are working around the clock to restore normal operations and have engaged with government cybersecurity teams,” said Chaiwat Rattanaporn, spokesperson for PayLink Thailand. “At this stage, we advise customers to carry cash and avoid large transactions online.”

The Bank of Thailand confirmed the incident, stating that no customer funds had been lost but warning that delays in payroll processing and bill payments could occur. “We are monitoring for signs of data leakage and will provide updates as more information becomes available,” said Deputy Governor Sunee Jirasak.

According to the Federation of Thai Industries, manufacturers in the Eastern Economic Corridor have experienced delays in supply shipments due to payment verification failures. The Thai Chamber of Commerce estimates that retail sales could fall by 20 percent today if the disruption continues.

“This attack exposes the vulnerability of our digital infrastructure,” said cybersecurity analyst Wongsakorn La-or. “Rapid recovery is crucial to limiting economic damage.”

Authorities have not attributed the attack to any group as investigations are ongoing.
